interaction: reactor H2 vent capacity vs column reflux: reactor gas side vs column top

diagnoses.summary: PCA shows a large coherent upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations. The fixed-rule evidence and contributions point to a reflux-side disturbance, most likely a failed reflux pump, causing abnormal drum holdup and temperature signals upstream of the reflux stage.
PCA shows large, coherent upset with reactor pressure rising and H2 vent involvement; likely H2 PCV fault causing pressure build-up and compensatory control activity.

Abnormal PCA: Large, coherent process upset with major pressure rise in the CSTR and high H2 vent activity. The most likely cause is a constraint on the H2 PCV (vent valve) leading to reactor pressure increase and compensatory flow changes at the CSTR outlet/vent path.

The PCA shows a large, coherent upset with both T² and SPE violations and high reactor pressure alarms. The leading evidence points to an H2 PCV (cstr_vent_valve) fault, most likely stuck-closed, with possible capacity degradation or a biased pressure sensor contributing secondarily.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with simultaneous SPE and T2 violations, dominated by reactor pressure rise driven by HYDROGEN PCV issue. Most likely a stuck-closed H2 PCV or degraded PCV capacity causing pressure buildup and compensatory controller action.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with both T² and SPE violated, dominated by CSTR pressure and H2 vent activity, with alarms showing reactor pressure high. The most consistent faults are related to the H2 PCV (vent valve) performance, causing pressure rise and compensatory loop action.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with both T² and SPE high, dominated by reactor pressure rise tied to the H2 purge/vent path. Alarms on reactor pressure (R_P_H, R_P_HH) point to an H2 PCV fault affecting venting. The top contributor is the cstr_pressure_bar driver with strong T² impact and substantial SPE contribution, consistent with PCV/controller action being unable to relieve pressure as commanded.

The abnormal PCA state with simultaneous T² and SPE violations, and alarms on reactor pressure (R_P_H, R_P_HH) point to a hydrogen purge/control valve issue at the CSTR. The fixed-rule hypotheses indicate the H2 PCV (pressure control valve) is not opening as commanded, causing elevated CSTR pressure and a coherent upset in the reactor variables.
PCA indicates a large, coherent upset dominated by CSTR temperature rise with high T2 and SPE violations; strongest evidence points to CSTR heater actuation anomaly driving the abnormal state.

PCA indicates a large, somewhat coherent upset with significant SPE, dominated by the CSTR pressure signal. Several faults point to H2 PCV issues or a biased reactor pressure measurement, with additional hints of condenser cooling loss. Most likely a combination of a degraded PCV performance and a biased pressure sensor driving the abnormal correlations.

The PCA shows a large, coherent upset with both T² and SPE violations, dominated by the reactor pressure measurement (meas.cstr_pressure_bar). The rule-based hypotheses point to H2 PCV (vent valve) issues as the primary cause, with a possible sensor bias contributing to the signal. The most likely root cause is a degraded or stuck H2 PCV, causing abnormal reactor pressure dynamics and driving the abnormal correlations observed.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with strong contribution from reactor pressure (CSTR pressure). The fixed-rule hypotheses point to H2 PCV issues as the primary driver, with additional possibility of PCV stiction or a biased pressure sensor.

The PCA monitor indicates a large, coherent plant upset with significant distortion in the normal correlations, with both T² and SPE violated. The strongest fault candidates point to the hydrogen PCV system affecting reactor pressure control.
Most likely a H2 PCV (PCV valve) fault causing reactor pressure rise with compensating control action; PCV likely stuck closed, with possible capacity degradation or sensor bias contributing.

PCA shows a large coherent shift with simultaneous SPE violation, dominated by the CSTR pressure signal, with secondary contributions from temperature and controller output. No active alarms or saturated loops detected. Likely a sensor fault driving apparent process upset, possibly combined with a H2 PCV issue.

PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with strong imbalance in CSTR variables, dominated by reactor temperature and pressure signals, with rule-based evidence pointing to a stuck/high heater condition in the CSTR as the most likely cause.

The PCA detects a large, coherent plant upset with both T² and SPE violated, dominated by the reactor temperature signal and a likely fault in the R_TIC path. The evidence points to a sensor fault affecting the R_TIC signal (and consequent heater/controller interaction), with possible secondary faults in the reactor heater and catalyst activity.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent upset dominated by reactor temperature with a likely heater issue and a suspicious TIC sensor reading drive the SPE. Most probable: reactor heater stuck high; second: sensor fault on op.R_TIC; possible contributing catalyst/activity/valve issues are less likely.

A large, coherent process upset with reactor temperature rising despite near-setpoint control suggests an actuator fault in the CSTR heater. The strongest rule-based hypothesis is reactor heater stuck high, with catalyst activity loss as a plausible secondary contributor.
Abnormal PCA: high coherence upset with large T2 and SPE violations, dominated by CSTR temperature. Fault hypotheses suggest a heater fault and/or catalyst activity loss driving the reactor upset.

PCA detects a large, coherent plant upset with strong temperature rise and controller action; multiple indicators point to a process upset rather than a pure sensor fault. The leading hypothesis is catalyst activity loss driving higher reactor temperature and pressure trends, with secondary possibilities including heater issues and PCV-related faults.
Abnormal, large coherent plant upset with high T2 and high SPE; strongest evidence points to CSTR heater fault causing elevated reactor temperature and related pressure rise.

PCA flags a large coherent plant upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations. The strongest rule-based hint points to a stuck high CSTR heater forcefully driving up reactor temperature, with secondary plausible faults in catalyst activity and H2 PCV behavior.

Both Hotelling T² and SPE are violated with a large coherent shift, dominated by reactor temperature and related control action. Rule-based hints point to heater-related and catalyst-related faults, with heater stuck/high-velocity compensation being the most likely primary issue.
